title: Finite triangulated realization cocone with completion normalization
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $X$ a Noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension on which $\ell$ is a unit in every stalk. Fix a CoefficientSystem $C$ of [lem-sf-locally-finite-adic-coefficient-system]. There are additive triangulated functors $\Phi_E$ from each raw finite-field rational constructible stage of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] to the derived category of native adic sheaves. For $E\le L$, isomorphisms $T_{L/E}\Phi_L\cong\Phi_E$ commute with shifts and satisfy the stage-system associator equation. On integral objects $\Phi_E$ followed by sections is naturally the derived extension along the integral map specified by $C$. The inverse scalar comparison on an integral object, after sections, equals the inverse derived balancing normalization followed by the completed-tensor comparison and these integral isomorphisms, with the literal-object transports retained. This is exactly FiniteCoconeData.normalized in the attached Lean module. No functor on the pair category or common-stage Hom quotient is asserted.

proof.text: Use [lem-fd-integral-identity-rational-equivalence] to identify the two raw rationalizations, with their actual integral localizations. Compose the finite continuous derived realization of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] with native scalar extension and the inverse section-module equivalence. Its integral comparison is the balanced tensor associator; the localization universal property extends its naturality from integral numerators to inverse uniformizer powers.

For $E\le L$, compose the inverse-completion scalar comparison with the normalized comparison in [lem-per-rational-realization-scalar-coherence] and derived tensor transitivity. Both successive-field composites flatten three scalar factors to their product. The scalar tower equations and the identity-rational comparison prove the displayed associator coherence, including repeated and ramified extensions. Constituent comparisons commute with shifts.

On an integral object the inverse scalar comparison is the completion-chain map followed by the same balanced tensor associator. Its normalized scalar equation is exactly FiniteCoconeData.normalized. Package the finite functors, shift data, integral comparisons and this equation. No pair-category descent is used.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteCocone_exists
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    [Fact (∃ n : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim X ≤ n)]
    [Fact (∀ x : X, IsUnit (l : X.presheaf.stalk x))]
    (C : CoefficientSystem l X) :
    letI := C.commutative
    letI := C.sectionsAdditive
    letI := C.sectionsLimits
    letI := C.sectionsColimits
    Nonempty (FiniteCocone l X C)
